# `sensor_mesh`

the good channels of one sensor type (MEG or EEG) as a surface whose vertices are those channels, chosen from the channels' type and quality labellings.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run sensor_mesh --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run sensor_mesh --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run sensor_mesh --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --channels <channels manifold> --sensor-type MEG|EEG [--name NAME] [--position-rule stored] [--cut 2]
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `channels` | manifold points, where {"name": "$channels"} (name the channels manifold (--channels)) | yes |
| `type` | selection set, manifold channels.manifold.0, where {"name": "$type_labelling"} (the channels' type labelling (the importer's montage family `type`)) | yes |
| `quality` | selection set, manifold channels.manifold.0, where {"name": "$quality_labelling"} (the channels' good/bad labelling (the importer's montage family `quality`: the recording's channel flags)) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | `--channels` | `required` | - |  | the channels manifold (a points manifold) by name |
| `sensor_type` | `--sensor-type` | `required` | - | MEG, EEG | which sensors are the vertices: MEG (MEG, MEG MAG, MEG GRAD; never MEG REF) or EEG; never both |
| `type_labelling` | `--type-labelling` | `type` | - |  | the channels' type labelling by name (the importer's montage family) |
| `quality_labelling` | `--quality-labelling` | `quality` | - |  | the channels' good/bad labelling by name (the importer's montage family) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{channels}_{sensor_type}_surface` | - |  | the surface's name; its map is <name>_map, its channels <name>_channels |
| `position_rule` | `--position-rule` | `brainstorm` | - | brainstorm, stored | a channel's position: brainstorm (the mean of its first coil_points coil points; its stored point without coils) or stored (its stored point) |
| `coil_points` | `--coil-points` | `4` | points |  | how many of a channel's first coil points are averaged (Brainstorm: 4) |
| `cut` | `--cut` | `2.0` | - |  | a triangle is removed when one of its edges is cut x the median edge or longer (nxr: 2) |
| `pole` | `--pole` | `[0, 0, 1]` | - |  | the projection's pole, a direction in the channels' coordinate system (nxr: +z) |
| `orientation` | `--orientation` | `outward` | - | outward, as_triangulated | each triangle turned so that its normal points away from the sensors' centroid (outward), or as_triangulated |
| `repair_passes` | `--repair-passes` | `20` | passes |  | the most passes of the pinch repair before refusing (nxr: 20) |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`meeg.good_channels_of_type`](../nodes.md) | type=type, quality=quality | sensor_type=$sensor_type | pick |
| before | [`meeg.channel_positions`](../nodes.md) | channels=channels, pick=pick | position_rule=$position_rule, coil_points=$coil_points | positions, channel_index |
| before | [`geometry.point_set_mesh`](../nodes.md) | points=positions | cut=$cut, pole=$pole, orientation=$orientation, repair_passes=$repair_passes | faces |
| before | [`geometry.surface_from_parts`](../nodes.md) | vertices=positions, faces=faces |  | surface |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `surface` | kind manifold, type surface, name $name, derived_from channels.manifold.0 |
| `channel_index` | kind field, kind_name channel map, name {name}_map, on surface |
| `pick` | kind selection, type indices, name {name}_channels, on channels.manifold.0 |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE SENSOR MESH: the good channels of one sensor type (MEG or EEG) as a surface, a triangulated helmet (MEG) or cap (EEG) whose vertices ARE those channels. The same surface as
`sensor_surface` makes, with the channels chosen from the channels' own labellings instead of a pick named by hand, so that importing a subject can make it with no hand step.
A manifold DERIVED from the channels: vertex i is the channel `<name>_map`[i] of the channels manifold, so a field on those channels is a field on the surface's vertices with
no mapping, and the channels get what any surface has (the intrinsic complex and its operators, the Hodge-Dirac modes: `run eigenmodes --surface <name>`).

THE GRAPH:  type, quality (the channels' labellings: a channel's type, e.g. MEG GRAD, and its quality, good or bad) --[meeg.good_channels_of_type]--> pick [m];
            channels, pick --[meeg.channel_positions]--> positions [m x 3], channel_index [m];  positions --[geometry.point_set_mesh]--> faces [F x 3];
            positions, faces --[geometry.surface_from_parts]--> surface.
Stored: the surface `<name>` (type surface, derived from the channels manifold; its producer records the sensor type, the labellings read, the position rule and the mesher's
options and report), the map `<name>_map` (an integer field on the surface: each vertex's channel) and the pick `<name>_channels` (an indices selection of the channels: the
surface's channels, so a cross-spectrum can be made on exactly them).
WHICH CHANNELS: the good channels of sensor_type, REQUIRED (MEG: MEG, MEG MAG and MEG GRAD, never MEG REF; EEG: EEG); MEG and EEG are never meshed together. Good channels only:
the recorded field is defined only there. Fewer than four is refused.
Positions: Brainstorm's rule by default (the mean of a channel's first four coil points: a CTF axial gradiometer's pickup coil), or the stored point (position_rule stored).
The mesh: the point-set mesher (the projection about the pole, the planar Delaunay, long chords cut, pinches and holes repaired, every triangle turned outward); a point in no
triangle is refused.

What it cannot resolve: the surface is a triangulation of the sensors, not a physical surface: its geometry is the sensors' layout (their spacing is its resolution: no pattern
shorter than about two sensor spacings is resolved on it), and a field on it is the sensors' measurement (lead fields, not cortical currents).

  nxr-neuro run sensor_mesh --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --channels <channels manifold> --sensor-type MEG|EEG [--name NAME] [--position-rule stored] [--cut 2]
```
